task: Find a FREE sub-hourly historical surface-obs feed for RJTT (Tokyo Haneda), the exact station Polymarket's Tokyo high-temp ladder settles on (per ref/pmkt_settlement_basis.md, wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT).
verdict_tier: sub-hourly, STRONGLY-PREFERRED tier per task rubric (10-min, 144 rows/day, clears the >=100 rows/day sub-hourly proof bar)
headline: JMA (Japan Meteorological Agency) publishes genuine 10-minute AMeDAS observations, including temperature, for the 'Haneda' (羽田) AMeDAS point at prec_no=44 / block_no=0371 -- lat 35°33.2'N, lon 139°46.8'E, elev 6m -- which sits essentially on top of Haneda Airport (RJTT: 35.5494N/139.7798E) and is the closest genuine JMA station to the Wunderground/Polymarket RJTT settlement station. Verified with real pulls for a recent day, a ~60-day-back day, and (bonus) a 1-year-back day: all three returned exactly 144 rows/day (00:10-24:00 JST, every 10 min). No API key, no account, no rate-limit gate encountered. Spot values cross-checked against IEM's independent RJTT METAR mirror at three separate hours, all within 0.1-0.3°C -- consistent with genuine station observations of the same physical site, not reanalysis or a different site. HISTORICAL availability is essentially same-day (a JST day's 144 rows become viewable as soon as that day is 'yesterday' in JST); REAL-TIME availability via this specific archive page is NOT live -- the page explicitly refuses today's (in-progress) JST day ('viewable dates are up to yesterday'), so a live deployment would need JMA's separate near-real-time AMeDAS distribution channel (not fully characterized in this run), not this historical-archive page.

station.jma_point_type: a (AMeDAS-only point: precipitation + temperature + wind measured; humidity and sunshine NOT measured at this point -- confirmed by the '///' columns and the onmouseover metadata flags '1,1,1,0,0,0')
station.distance_note: JMA's block_no=0371 'Haneda' AMeDAS point coordinates (35.553N/139.780E) are ~0.3km from RJTT's published aerodrome reference point (35.5494N/139.7798E) -- effectively the same site/airport, not a proxy from a different city location. JMA does not publish a separate point literally labeled 'RJTT' or an ICAO code; 'Haneda' (block_no=0371) is JMA's own AMeDAS designation for this airport site.
station.settlement_basis_confirmed: matches ref/pmkt_settlement_basis.md row: Polymarket Tokyo high-temp ladder cites 'Tokyo Haneda Airport Station', wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT -- prior study measured 14/14 (100%) agreement between IEM's RJTT METAR daily extreme and the settled Polymarket bracket, so this JMA co-located station carries the same settlement-basis soundness

candidates_checked.name: JMA (Japan Meteorological Agency) 10-minute AMeDAS historical viewer (data.jma.go.jp/stats/etrn)
candidates_checked.cadence_verified: 10-min (144 obs/day: :00... every 10 minutes from 00:10 through 24:00 JST)
candidates_checked.auth: none -- fully open HTTP GET, no API key, no account, no cookies/session required
candidates_checked.rate_limits: none documented; informal politeness expected (this run: ~9 sequential GETs to data.jma.go.jp at roughly 1/sec with pauses, no throttling, no errors, no CAPTCHA)
candidates_checked.licensing: Japan's '公共データ利用規約（第1.0版）' (Public Data License v1.0) applies to JMA website content per jma.go.jp/jma/kishou/info/coment.html -- free to use/redistribute, ATTRIBUTION REQUIRED (cite '出典：気象庁ホームページ' + the page URL; if content is edited/processed, must also disclose that it was processed and must not present it as if produced by the government). No login gate, no paid tier, no explicit anti-scraping clause found; robots.txt at data.jma.go.jp returns 404 (path not present) so no machine-readable crawl restriction was found for this subdomain either.
candidates_checked.history_depth_verified_days: 365+ (recent day 2026-07-21, ~60-day-back 2026-05-24, AND a full 1-year-back day 2026-07-23/2025-07-23 all returned complete 144-row days; not exhaustively tested further back, but the site's own '前年' (previous year) navigation link on the day page implies multi-year archive depth beyond what was pulled here)
candidates_checked.realtime_lag_note: Historical (backtest) availability is same-day: a completed JST calendar day's full 144-row table is retrievable via this page as soon as JMA considers that day to be 'yesterday' or earlier -- pulling the CURRENT in-progress JST day (2026-07-24, tested live) returned an explicit error page stating '閉覧可能な日は、昨日2026年7月23日までです' ("viewable dates are up to yesterday, 2026-07-23") -- i.e. this specific archive endpoint does NOT serve any data for the day still in progress, only fully-completed prior days. This is a historical-archive characteristic, not a live feed; the historical side (what unblocks the backtest) is effectively unblocked with near-zero lag once a day completes. Real-time/live signal generation would need a DIFFERENT JMA channel (their public AMeDAS map draws from a near-real-time JSON feed at www.jma.go.jp/bosai/amedas/... on ~10min cadence, matching the observation interval) -- NOT independently pulled/verified in this run; flagged as the next step if live deployment on this feed is pursued, per GROUNDING non-negotiable #5 (latency is part of the signal definition, note real-time separately from historical).
candidates_checked.request_note: This is an HTML table page (not a CSV/JSON API) -- requires simple regex/HTML-table parsing (<tr>/<td>) to extract rows; no query-string content-type switch was found to get raw CSV directly from this endpoint. Columns in order: 時分 (JST time, 10-min steps), 降水量(mm) (precip), 気温(℃) (temp), 相対湿度(%) (humidity, '///' = not measured at this point), 風向・風速 平均/最大瞬間 (avg wind dir/speed, max gust dir/speed), 日照時間(min) (sunshine, '///' = not measured at this point). Station navigation: prefecture map at select/prefecture00.php?prec_no=44 -> prefecture.php?prec_no=44&block_no=&... (station map with per-point <area> tags) -> the day/element menu at ../index.php?prec_no=44&block_no=0371&year=YYYY&month=M&day=D&view= -> the 10-min table itself at view/10min_a1.php with the same params.

candidates_checked.name: Synoptic Data free tier
candidates_checked.status: NOT pulled -- token-gated, unlikely to beat JMA's own 10-min direct feed for a Japanese domestic station

candidates_checked.name: Open-Meteo historical archive
candidates_checked.reason: Open-Meteo's historical endpoint is ERA5/model reanalysis, not station observations -- explicitly excluded by the task's own rule ('reanalysis does NOT count'). Not pulled.

candidates_checked.name: JMA real-time AMeDAS JSON distribution (www.jma.go.jp/bosai/amedas/...)
candidates_checked.status: NOT independently pulled/verified this run -- flagged for a live-deployment follow-up, not needed to establish the HISTORICAL verdict
candidates_checked.reason: This is the channel JMA's own public AMeDAS map draws from for near-real-time (~10-min cadence) point data, distinct from the historical-archive HTML pages verified above (which explicitly refuse the in-progress day, see realtime_lag_note). Historical availability -- the blocker this feedhunt exists to unblock -- is already established via the verified archive pages; live/real-time cadence for this specific station was not characterized in this run and should be confirmed separately before any live signal design relies on it, per GROUNDING non-negotiable #5.

verification_method.sub_hourly_threshold_note: 144 rows/day is genuine 10-min cadence, clearing the task's '>=100 rows/day proves sub-hourly' bar comfortably and landing in the 'strongly preferred' 10-min-or-better tier, not just the 'marginal' 30-min tier.
verification_method.plausibility_verdict: All three independently-sourced spot comparisons (JMA AMeDAS 10-min vs IEM's RJTT METAR mirror, same UTC instant converted to JST) agree within 0.1-0.3°C -- well within the expected rounding/instrument/exact-minute-offset noise between a whole-METAR-report and a 10-min-interval AMeDAS reading, and consistent with the two feeds reading the same physical airport site rather than different stations or a model output.

realtime_vs_historical_lag.historical_availability: same-day-or-better -- once a JST calendar day is complete, its full 144-row table is retrievable via the archive page with no observed further delay (the 365-day-back, 60-day-back and 2-day-back pulls were all identical in structure/completeness)
realtime_vs_historical_lag.realtime_availability: NOT usable via this archive page -- the in-progress JST day returns an explicit 'not viewable yet, only through yesterday' error (verified live against the actual current day, 2026-07-24 JST, which had 0 rows at query time 07:41 JST). A live deployment needs JMA's separate near-real-time AMeDAS JSON channel, not characterized in this run.

auth_summary: No API key, no account, no login required for the winning feed (JMA data.jma.go.jp 10-min AMeDAS archive pages) or its cross-check source (IEM asos.py for RJTT METAR). Both are anonymous HTTP GET.
rate_limits_summary: No documented hard rate limit found for data.jma.go.jp. This session made ~9 sequential GETs to JMA endpoints at roughly 1/sec with pauses (plus a handful to IEM), no throttling, no errors, no CAPTCHA. Continued politeness (sequential, ~1 req/sec, cache-then-reuse) recommended per GROUNDING.md non-negotiable #8.
licensing_summary: JMA's data.jma.go.jp content falls under Japan's Public Data License v1.0 (公共データ利用規約、第1.0版) per jma.go.jp/jma/kishou/info/coment.html: free to use and redistribute, requires source attribution ('出典：気象庁ホームページ' + URL), and if processed/edited must disclose that and must not present the result as government-produced. No paid tier, no scraping prohibition found (robots.txt path returns 404). This is the same station Polymarket's own settlement page (Wunderground) displays for Tokyo -- the JMA feed is the ORIGINATING national-agency data for that airport site, one step upstream of both Wunderground and the METAR/IEM mirror.
relevance_to_grounding_blocker: ref/GROUNDING.md and ref/pmkt_final_verdict.md's STILL-BLOCKED verdict cite 'hourly METAR... under-reports the diurnal peak by ~1h of temperature change' as the coverage blocker for the 5 non-US whitelist cities including Tokyo. This feedhunt found that RJTT/Haneda has a genuinely finer free national-agency feed (JMA 10-min AMeDAS, 144 obs/day) that is 6x denser than the 24/day the prior study's IEM report_type=3-only pull assumed, and even 3x denser than the 48/day 30-min METAR/SPECI cadence found for RJTT here and for EGLC in the prior London feedhunt. Re-running the coverage/signal-fire analysis for Tokyo with this 10-min JMA feed (not just the METAR mirror) is a natural, cheap next step flagged for a follow-up study -- not claimed as resolved here, since this run only verifies feed existence/cadence/plausibility, not coverage-rate impact.
